turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, select the 5
candidates with the LARGEST SHG tensor component |d_ij| (pm/V) that also
satisfy a transparency requirement: the band gap must be at least 3 eV. Band
gaps are NOT given for the pool -- you must infer them. A selected candidate
whose band gap is below the threshold scores zero.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The SHG tensor vanishes by symmetry in any centrosymmetric crystal, so only non-centrosymmetric candidates can be competitive. Among the remaining structures the magnitude of the largest \(|d_{ij}|\) is controlled by (i) the polarizability of the anion, (ii) the degree of alignment of the polarizable anionic units (tetrahedra or lone-pair pyramids), and (iii) the optical dielectric constant, all of which increase as the band gap decreases. Consequently the optimal materials sit just above the 3 eV transparency threshold and contain the heaviest chalcogen that still satisfies that threshold.

Compositional interpolation of well-known binaries and ternaries (LiGaSe\(_2\) \(E_g=3.34\) eV, MgSe \(E_g\approx3.6\) eV) places every Li–Mg–Ga–Se adamantine phase comfortably above 3 eV, while the corresponding Zn analogues and all heavier-cation selenides/tellurides fall below the cutoff. The same family is built from aligned GaSe\(_4\) tetrahedra, giving a large constructive contribution to \(d_{ij}\). Within the family the five densest (hence highest-\(n\)) members are the monoclinic Li\(_2\)MgGa\(_2\)Se\(_5\) realizations; their volumes per formula unit increase in the order c094 < c097 < c098 < c095 < c096, which is therefore the expected ranking of \(|d_{ij}|\).

All other non-centrosymmetric candidates that meet the gap requirement (wurtzite/zinc-blende SiC polytypes, BeSe, ZnGa\(_2\)S\(_4\), LiAlS\(_2\), thioborates, etc.) contain lighter anions or less polarizable bonds and therefore possess systematically smaller tensors.

Final: c094, c097, c098, c095, c096
